bug_semantics: The remotely reachable /uploadFile multipart handler used the request-controlled sid and uploaded item name as the child path below its upload directory without validating or canonicalizing either value. A sid containing parent-directory components therefore escaped the intended upload directory; choosing a JSP upload name let an unauthenticated attacker place executable content in a web-accessible location and then request it.
flaw_origin: Direct feature commit 7436c2f0b67128a558e3ac3a820ef8e0a01f59c0 created the upload handler, exposed /uploadFile, and first wrote the vulnerable File(parent, request.getParameter("sid") + "_" + item.getName()) sink. Later moves, package renames, and the 2022 FileUtils storage refactor preserved that trust decision and are not introducers.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 7436c2f0b67128a558e3ac3a820ef8e0a01f59c0 shows human author and committer pavel-miniutka <asphalt.by@gmail.com>, the sole message '[Web]: file upload', no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and no bot identity.
evidence: The first-party issue https://github.com/lsfusion/platform/issues/1544 identifies lsFusion <= 6.1, UploadFileRequestHandler.handleRequest, the /uploadFile API, unvalidated sid concatenation with FileUtils.APP_UPLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, unrestricted uploaded names, and a demonstrated traversal-assisted JSP upload/RCE path. The assigned GitHub advisory GHSA-gwwr-j923-vq7r / CVE-2025-13262 independently classifies the sid behavior as CWE-22 and records the affected Maven range as <= 6.1.

In the validated clone, git show 7436c2f0b67128a558e3ac3a820ef8e0a01f59c0 adds platform/web-api/src/main/java/platform/gwt/base/server/handlers/UploadFileHandler.java. Its lines 24-31 parse multipart items and pass request.getParameter("sid") + "_" + item.getName() directly to new File(request.getRealPath("WEB-INF/temp"), ...), then item.write(file). The same commit adds the fileUploadHandler bean and maps it to /uploadFile in platform/web-client/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml; its security configuration protects only /form.jsp and the GWT form RPC path, not /uploadFile.

The BIC parent is direct and fully verified: git cat-file -p 7436c2f0b67128a558e3ac3a820ef8e0a01f59c0 names parent be5f2d4b7523e6d2178c9ef56205c24d3389f71f; git diff-tree --name-status on that edge reports the handler as A; git cat-file -e parent:platform/web-api/src/main/java/platform/gwt/base/server/handlers/UploadFileHandler.java fails because the path does not exist; and git grep -E 'uploadFile|fileUploadHandler|ServletFileUpload' on the parent has no matches, while the child has the handler, clients, bean, and route.

History cross-checks converge on the same smallest origin. git log -L 24,31:platform/web-api/src/main/java/platform/gwt/base/server/handlers/UploadFileHandler.java at 7436c2f0b67128a558e3ac3a820ef8e0a01f59c0 attributes the complete parse/concatenate/write block to that new-file commit. git log -S 'request.getParameter("sid") + "_" + item.getName()' on the original path finds 7436c2f0b67128a558e3ac3a820ef8e0a01f59c0 as the earliest addition. git log --follow on the present UploadFileRequestHandler path reaches that commit through the later renames. In particular, 9c61e52693e3dcf02d794bc05d6e8aacce08590c merely replaced item.write with FileUtils.writeFile while preserving the unvalidated composite name, and cf725e7a33d07e6a176e29b812d95fd6ed57be7b only enabled overwrite.

The direct closing commit e257d15e55eefdcd1606c6a041e19a8bd1f74fde, titled 'Fixed arbitrary file upload (closes #1544)', reads sid once, rejects any sid containing '..' with HTTP 400, and only then supplies sid + '_' + item.getName() to FileUtils.writeFile. Its v6 cherry-pick 35248bf209dc32755ee529da2cb1e66f373ab69c states '(cherry picked from commit e257d15e55eefdcd1606c6a041e19a8bd1f74fde)'; the fixed handler blobs are identical, and both descend from the BIC.

Release-tree verification establishes the boundary: tag 6.1 resolves to cbbef9c5ac9ea6365164cd94914026d608ea832d and still contains the direct unvalidated request.getParameter("sid") write; neither fix commit is its ancestor. Tag 6.2 resolves to dd4dbe5bf9b136e73e18fe25d741253929324350, contains v6 fix 35248bf209dc32755ee529da2cb1e66f373ab69c, and shows the '..' rejection. git tag --contains the BIC starts at 1.0.0 and includes every numbered release through 6.1; git tag --contains each fix reports 6.2, so the repository's first fixed release is 6.2, consistent with the advisory's <= 6.1 affected boundary.

BIC-only AI inspection used the raw commit object, not the issue, fix, branch, or later history: git cat-file -p 7436c2f0b67128a558e3ac3a820ef8e0a01f59c0 reports author and committer pavel-miniutka <asphalt.by@gmail.com> at 2013-02-07, message '[Web]: file upload', no trailers, and no bot identity.
reasoning: The vulnerability began with the upload feature itself: the same atomic 2013 commit created a remotely mapped multipart endpoint and let both sid and the client filename determine the filesystem destination without containment validation. Its immediate parent has neither an upload endpoint nor an equivalent multipart sink, so causal parent absence is proven. The later file moves and 2022 switch to FileUtils changed representation and storage plumbing but retained the already-vulnerable composite pathname; choosing any of them would mistake a carrier for the BIC. The vulnerable state remained in the 6.1 release. The default-branch fix e257d15e55eefdcd1606c6a041e19a8bd1f74fde rejects the advisory's traversal primitive, and its byte-equivalent v6 cherry-pick is present in the first subsequent release, 6.2. Because the only permitted AI evidence source is the BIC commit object and that object has a human identity with no AI attribution or bot marker, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
